statement: For iid passage times equal to a fixed c>=0 on every nearest-neighbor edge of Z^2, the horizontal path v_k=(k,0), k in Z, is a bi-infinite geodesic.
assumptions: Passage-time law is the point mass at finite c>=0
proof: Between (i,0) and (j,0), every path has at least |j-i| edges, so has weight at least c|j-i|; the horizontal subpath has exactly that weight. This remains true at c=0.
remaining_gap: No mathematical gap identified; independent review pending. This refutes only an extension permitting constant laws, not P0117's nonatomic-law target.

statement: For iid finite nonnegative nonconstant edge weights on Z^2, almost surely no global geodesic ray is eventually contained in any finite horizontal or vertical strip. For S_w=Z x {-w,...,w}, choose 0<=a<b with p=P(t<=a)>0 and r=P(t>=b)>0, put L=floor(a(4w+2)/(b-a))+1 and q=r^((2w+1)L)*p^(L+4w+2). The probability that a global finite geodesic connects some vertex in column 0 to some vertex in column n while staying in S_w is at most (1-q)^floor((n+1)/(L+1)).
proof: Prescribe expensive horizontal strip edges in disjoint finite blocks and cheap exterior-row detours with boundary-column connectors. Cut counting gives crossing cost >=bL, while the detour costs <=a(L+4w+2)<bL. Successful blocks have probability q and disjoint deterministic edge supports. Any strip-contained crossing would force every full block to fail. Positive-probability barriers recur in both directions; an injective strip-confined ray has unbounded horizontal coordinate. Take countable unions over widths, shifts, starts and rotations.
remaining_gap: Independent mathematical review pending. This controls deterministic finite strips; it supplies no confinement theorem for arbitrary bigeodesics.

statement: For iid weights equal to a>0 with probability p in (0,1) and b>a otherwise, if northeast oriented bond percolation on the a-edges has positive forward survival probability theta(p), then almost surely there exists a bi-infinite global FPP geodesic.
assumptions: Positive northeast directed open-ray survival probability theta(p)

source.external_instantiation: Primary source for the supercritical oriented-percolation regime is being checked.

proof: Forward and backward open-ray events at the origin depend on disjoint time-level edge sets and each has probability theta(p), so their intersection has probability theta(p)^2. Concatenated rays are injective and coordinatewise monotone. Each finite segment has Manhattan distance many a-edges; any competitor costs at least that Manhattan distance times a. Translation invariance and iid ergodicity imply existence somewhere almost surely.
remaining_gap: Independent review and primary-source instantiation of theta(p)>0 pending. This is a counterexample only to an atomic extension; it does not refute P0117.

statement: An axis-asymptotic bi-infinite global FPP geodesic need not have either tail in a finite horizontal strip: in the constant weight-1 environment, the monotone staircase through (k,sign(k)*floor(sqrt(abs(k)))) has end directions +/-e1 and unbounded transverse displacement at both ends.
assumptions: The proposed bridge relies only on having axis end directions
proof: The staircase consists only of east and north steps, hence every finite segment is Manhattan optimal. Its transverse coordinate is unbounded but sublinear in its longitudinal coordinate, so its end directions are axial while it escapes every finite strip.
remaining_gap: Independent review pending. This is a geometric/constant-law counterexample, not a nonatomic iid counterexample or a refutation of P0117.
